All the places looked good and if I used a twister spinner, either my left foot would fall on the dosa place or my right hand on the poke bowl place. But my eyes were set on empanadas. the menu was promising and was surprised with two things. First, i'm a sucker for coca cola in a bottle. But whatever, the second surprise was that after I placed my order, the dude said it would take 12-13 minutes. I was like say what? I went along. I didn't have to be anywhere. So I saw him baste the empanadas with butter and pop them in the ...

I can't say for sure, but I think this is the first time I've had an empanada. That doesn't sound right, but at the very least I have no memory as having eaten one. So take this review with whatever weight you deem appropriate. I will start with the stuffings I got, which were crawfish etouffee and the gumbo. Obviously went with Louisiana version and not the traditional because that's what I felt like in the moment. Both of those were very good. It was a bit messy since both of my stuffings were of the soupish variety, but who in Nola is scared of a 5 napkin food. My next thought about the empanada here was how soft, crumbly, and crispy the dough was. It simultaneously crisped on the bite...

Hot awesome Argentinian style empanadas. Location is great inside the Auction House Market. There is multiple options, Latin options include Mexican chorizo and Argentinian beef or Peruvian chicken, New Orleans options which include Gumbo and crawfish, the other options are beef bourguignon(which I liked a lot), a mushroom and cheese, and ratatouille to name a few. My favorite ones are the Latin ones as they have a lot of flavor. The crawfish option was delicious as well as the mushroom option. I say also try their 2 sauces which pair well with different options. Like the green creamy sauce goes well with crawfish, the spicy one goes well the Argentinian option and then the beef bourguign...
